pages.title: Wōkerer
pages.hint: A byname heard on the quay
pages.brief: The usurer: a man who lends silver and takes back more. It is what your creditor is called on the quay.
pages.game: Your creditor is called the Wōkerer, though not to his face. You owe him the price of your boat by the day he named. If the silver is short on that day he takes her back, with whatever lies in her.
pages.known:
From wōker, usury: silver grown from silver. Old Frisian wōker is a recorded word, beside Old English wōcor and Old High German wuohhar, and it lives on as Dutch woeker and German Wucher. The ending that makes it a man's byname is the game's own, after the Low German wôkerer of later centuries (?).
The Church forbade usury to its clergy at Nicaea in 325, and the assembly at Aachen in 789 declared it wrong for laymen too. Usury then meant any price at all for a loan. So your creditor does not lend: he sold you a boat on a tally for more than she is worth, which is allowed, and the quay calls him by the name all the same.
pages.source: A placeholder page, written with the opening on 7 October 2026. Checked on 8 October: Old Frisian wōker (Wiktionary, Proto-Germanic *wōkraz, descendants); the council of Aix of 789 on laymen (Catholic Encyclopedia, Usury). Not checked: the byname's own ending.
